chunks: The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who entered Ramadan while he was ill and unable to fast, and he died in the month of Ramadan or in the month of Shawwal. He said: 'There is no fasting upon him, nor is it compensated on his behalf.' I said: 'And a postpartum woman who entered Ramadan and was unable to fast, and she died in the month of Ramadan or in the month of Shawwal?' He said: 'It is not compensated on her behalf.'
ai.seo_question: Do the deceased need to make up missed fasts from Ramadan if they died while ill or postpartum?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfabar highlights the Shia juristic consensus that valid excuses for fasting, such as illness or postpartum bleeding, are excused permanently upon death, distinguishing this from temporary absences. It clarifies that no fasting (sawm) or compensation (qada) is due from the deceased's estate, emphasizing the mercy of divine law in relieving believers of unfulfilled obligations when death occurs before recovery. This ruling underscores the principle that the burden of worship is lifted once the capacity to fulfill it is permanently lost.
